about: Mutants of compiler/check/bind, the self-hosted checker's collect and bind (capstone S3b). The laws (TestCompilerBindLawsRun) or the agreement with the Go checker over the corpus (TestCompilerBindAgreesWithChecker) kill each.

mutants.name: release-keeps-shadow
mutants.rule: A scope's end gives each name back to the binding it shadowed.

mutants.name: define-forgets-shadowed
mutants.rule: A local remembers the binding it shadows, so the outer one returns when its scope ends.

mutants.name: resolve-skips-locals
mutants.rule: The innermost local of a name wins over the package's declaration.

mutants.name: resolve-drops-file-base
mutants.rule: A package declaration's PNode is its file's base plus its row: files are laid end to end.

mutants.name: params-not-declared
mutants.rule: A function's parameters are locals of its body.

mutants.name: param-where-walked
mutants.to:
opt(b, f.Type)
					opt(b, f.Where)
					for j
mutants.rule: A parameter's where clause is the refinement type the checker derives; its names are that type's, so bind records none.

mutants.name: case-name-always-binds
mutants.rule: In a case, a name that names a type (the package's, the universe's or the prelude's) tests the value; it binds nothing.

mutants.name: later-alternative-redeclares
mutants.rule: The alternatives of a case bind one set of names; the first alternative's rows declare them.

mutants.name: with-head-skips-locals
mutants.rule: A local named in a with head is a use the checker records.

mutants.name: with-head-records-contexts
mutants.rule: A package context named bare in a with or within head is the context pass's: the checker records no use.

mutants.name: former-recorded
mutants.rule: Map and wired are predeclared formers: the checker records no object for them.

mutants.name: prelude-type-binds
mutants.rule: The prelude's types test in a case as the package's types do.

mutants.name: derive-qualifier-dropped
mutants.from:
case syntax.Name:
			use(b, e.X)
			selector(b, e.X, e.Sel)
		case _:
			qualifiers(b, e.X)
mutants.to:
case syntax.Name:
			selector(b, e.X, e.Sel)
		case _:
			qualifiers(b, e.X)
mutants.rule: A derive clause records the imports it qualifies with and the names it reads from them, and nothing else.

mutants.name: operations-out-of-law-scope
mutants.rule: An operation type's laws call its operations by their bare names.

mutants.name: functype-params-used
mutants.from:
no body: nothing can name them.
		let pm = mark(*b)
		params(b, dense.OptOf(ft.Params))
		release(b, pm)
mutants.to:
no body: nothing can name them.
		children(b, ft.Params)
mutants.rule: A function type's parameter names are declarations, not uses.

mutants.name: operation-params-undeclared
mutants.rule: An operation's parameters are declared (a Def of the checker), in a scope with no body.

mutants.name: context-entry-included-used
mutants.rule: A bare entry of a context includes another context: the context pass's, no use.

mutants.name: package-let-pattern-binds
mutants.rule: A package-level pattern let's names are the store's declarations, not locals.

mutants.name: parent-written-overcounts
mutants.rule: The parent column writes one entry per row that is a child: the rows less the files.

mutants.name: parent-base-dropped
mutants.rule: A child's PNode is its file's base plus its row.

mutants.name: rowof-first-file
mutants.rule: RowOf finds the file whose base range holds the PNode.

mutants.name: print-kinds-only
mutants.from: writeToken(&b, k, if k == syntax.Semicolon { "" } else { syntax.TokText(p, j) })
mutants.rule: A print hashes each token's text as well as its kind.

mutants.name: print-sees-positions
mutants.rule: A print does not see positions: a declaration moved or relaid keeps its prints.

mutants.name: print-semicolon-text
mutants.rule: A semicolon counts by its kind alone: one written and one the scanner inserts are one token.

mutants.name: ifp-no-cut
mutants.from: let inCut = at >= cutLo && at < cutHi
mutants.to: let inCut = at >= cutLo && at < cutHi && false
mutants.rule: The interface print cuts a non-generic function's body.

mutants.name: ifp-cuts-generic
mutants.rule: A generic function's body is in its interface print: an importer instantiates it.

mutants.name: ifp-test-uncut
mutants.rule: A test's body is cut from its interface print.

mutants.name: pattern-let-unprinted
mutants.rule: A package pattern let's declarations get their declaration's prints.

mutants.name: local-def-unmarked
mutants.rule: Every local's declaring row is a Def.

mutants.name: law-name-undeclared
mutants.rule: A law's name is a Def in no scope.

mutants.name: child-start-shifted
mutants.rule: A row's children in the column are the tree's children, from the row's start to the next row's.

mutants.name: with-filter-misses-with
mutants.rule: Every call whose first token is with takes the view path, where a with head's bare package context is no use.

mutants.name: overlay-remap-skipped
mutants.from: let id = if e.name.over { remap[dense.Index(e.name.id)] } else { e.name.id }
mutants.rule: The join maps a body's overlay names to the package's names it interns them as (C0/plan.md §3.2).

mutants.name: join-reverse-order
mutants.to:
for i in 0..len(bodies) {
		let body = bodies[len(bodies)-1-i]
mutants.rule: The join takes the bodies in canonical order, never another (the nearest writable form of join-by-completion-order: tasks.Transform gives its results in input order).

mutants.name: overlay-not-tagged
mutants.rule: A name the package's frozen names lack is the body overlay's, not a package id.

mutants.name: split-drops-last
mutants.rule: The pieces cover every top-level row.

mutants.name: overlay-text-unrecorded
mutants.rule: A body records each overlay text it interns, in order, for the join.

mutants.name: ifp-always-fp
mutants.rule: Only a declaration with nothing cut has its Fp as its Ifp.

mutants.name: ifp-body-kept
mutants.rule: The interface print leaves out the bytes of the cut span's tokens.

mutants.name: bind-go-import-unread
mutants.rule: import go PATH (the go word as its NamePos, no name) is a Go import, not an Ergo package of that path: std strings imports go strings, and binding it as itself cuts every import of strings.
